items.title: Section: Excellent Mind's Own Meditative Stability, and Excellent Wisdom Named From the Very Wisdom That Observes Reality

items.zh: 云何菩薩增上心住？謂諸菩薩，增上戒住清淨為緣，所得世間靜慮、等持、等至住。云何菩薩覺分相應增上慧住？謂諸菩薩，以世間淨智所依等持為所依止，為覺諸諦，於正念住等三十七菩提分法妙簡擇住。
items.en:
What is a bodhisattva's abode of excellent mind? It is the abode where, taking the purity of excellent moral discipline as its condition, a bodhisattva abides in the worldly meditative absorption, concentration, and attainment thereby obtained.
What is a bodhisattva's abode of excellent wisdom associated with the factors of awakening? It is the abode where, relying on the concentration that underlies worldly, pure wisdom, in order to awaken to the truths, a bodhisattva abides in the wondrous discernment cultivated through the thirty-seven factors of awakening, beginning with the foundations of mindfulness.

items.title: Section: The Truths Themselves Give the Fifth Ground Its Name, and Dependent Origination's Flow and Stilling Give the Sixth

items.zh: 云何菩薩諸諦相應增上慧住？謂諸菩薩，覺分簡擇為所依止，於諸諦中如實覺住。云何菩薩緣起流轉止息相應增上慧住？謂諸菩薩，於諦能覺增上力故，簡擇顯示由無智故，苦及因起；簡擇顯示由有智故，苦及因滅住。
items.en:
What is a bodhisattva's abode of excellent wisdom associated with the truths? It is the abode where, relying on the discernment already cultivated through the factors of awakening, a bodhisattva abides in genuine, correct realisation with respect to the truths.
What is a bodhisattva's abode of excellent wisdom associated with the stilling of the flow of dependent origination? It is the abode where, through the power of realising the truths, a bodhisattva discerns and reveals that, through lack of wisdom, suffering and its cause arise; and discerns and reveals that, through the presence of wisdom, suffering and its cause cease.
Commentary: Regarding "through lack of wisdom, suffering and its cause arise" and the like — lack of wisdom here means ignorance. Suffering means the links of birth and of ageing-and-death. The remaining links of dependent origination, since they are capable of producing suffering, harbouring its seed within themselves, are all called cause. This meaning is as explained in the Stage With Both Investigation and Analysis. This is called the flow of dependent origination. Its opposite is called the presence of wisdom, whereby suffering and its cause cease — this is called the stilling of dependent origination.

items.title: Section: The Seventh Ground's Effortful Mark-Free Abiding, and the Eighth Ground's Effortless, Spontaneous Version of the Same

items.zh: 云何菩薩有加行有功用無相住？謂諸菩薩，即由三種增上慧住增上力故，有加行、有功用、無缺無間，於一切法真如無分別慧修俱行住。云何菩薩無加行無功用無相住？謂諸菩薩，即於前無相住多修習已，任運自然、無缺無間運轉道隨行住。
items.en:
What is a bodhisattva's mark-free abode with effortful application? It is the abode where, through the combined power of the three abodes of excellent wisdom, a bodhisattva abides joined with effortful, applied, uninterrupted cultivation of the non-discriminating wisdom realising the suchness of all phenomena.
Commentary: Regarding "the suchness of all phenomena" and the like — the selflessness of all phenomena is called the suchness of all phenomena. Taking this as the condition, realising that not the slightest phenomenon or category of phenomena can any longer give rise to discrimination, observing all phenomena with genuine, equal, undiscriminating accuracy, is called non-discriminating wisdom. Because, within this abode, the practice of applied effort has reached its own completion, this is called cultivation joined with practice.
What is a bodhisattva's abode without marks and without effortful application? It is this same abode, mark-free abiding already thoroughly cultivated, now spontaneous and natural, continuing without interruption along this same path.

items.title: Section: The Ninth Ground's Boundless Retention and Unobstructed Eloquence, and the Tenth Ground's Reception of the Great Dharma-Consecration — Closing All Ten Abodes' Own Defining Nature

items.zh: 云何菩薩無礙解住？謂諸菩薩即以善清淨無動慧等持為所依止，得廣大慧，為他說法；無上為依，能於諸法異門、義趣、釋詞、差別妙簡擇住。云何菩薩最上成滿菩薩住？謂諸菩薩安住於此，於菩薩道已到究竟，於阿耨多羅三藐三菩提已得大法灌頂，或一生所繫，或居最後有。從此住無間，即於爾時證覺無上正等菩提，能作一切佛所作事。
items.en:
What is a bodhisattva's abode of unobstructed understanding? It is the abode where, relying on the genuinely pure, unmoving wisdom and concentration already attained, a bodhisattva obtains vast wisdom for teaching others; and, grounded in this unsurpassed capacity, abides in the wondrous discernment of the varied approaches, meaning, explanatory terms, and distinctions of all phenomena.
Commentary: Regarding "obtains vast wisdom" and the like — this means giving rise to applied wisdom with respect to all phenomena, able to teach every kind of teaching to others, genuinely knowing everything involved in every kind of teaching activity — this is called obtaining vast wisdom for teaching others. Obtaining boundless gateways of mnemonic retention, thoroughly and skilfully analysing every kind of phonetic and verbal element, with inexhaustible eloquence — this is called grounded in this unsurpassed capacity, down through wondrous discernment.
What is a bodhisattva's most excellent, fully accomplished bodhisattva abode? It is the abode where a bodhisattva, abiding here, has brought the bodhisattva path to its own ultimate completion, has already received the great dharma-consecration towards unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening, and is either bound to only one more life or already abides in the very last existence. From this abode, without interval, at that very moment, such a bodhisattva realises unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening, thereby able to perform every deed a buddha performs.

items.title: Section: How Cultivation of the Six Perfections Itself Grows in Scope — Narrow at Resolute Practice, Vast From the First Ground, Immeasurable From the Seventh

items.zh: 又諸菩薩勝解行住，於菩薩修所作狹小、所作有缺、所作不定，所得有退。極歡喜住，於菩薩修所作廣大、所作無缺、所作決定，隨所獲得無復退轉。如極歡喜住，乃至三種增上慧住，應知亦爾。從初無相住乃至最上成滿菩薩住，於菩薩修所作無量、所作無缺、所作決定，隨所獲得終無退轉。
items.en:
Furthermore, bodhisattvas at the abode of resolute practice, with respect to a bodhisattva's own cultivation, find it narrow in scope, incomplete in execution, and inconstant, so that whatever is attained can regress.
Commentary: Regarding "a bodhisattva's own cultivation" — this refers to the six perfections, one should understand.
At the abode of utmost joy, with respect to a bodhisattva's own cultivation, it becomes vast in scope, complete without gaps, and settled, so that whatever is attained never again regresses. One should understand that the same holds from the abode of utmost joy through the three abodes of excellent wisdom.
From the first mark-free abode through the most excellent, fully accomplished bodhisattva abode, with respect to a bodhisattva's own cultivation, it becomes immeasurable in scope, complete without gaps, and settled, so that whatever is attained is never lost.

items.title: Section: The Five Stages of Mark-Free Cultivation — Setting Forth, Attaining, Fully Realising, Purifying, and Finally Receiving Its Fruit

items.zh: 又諸菩薩勝解行住，於菩薩無相修，當知發趣。極歡喜住、增上戒住、增上心住、增上慧住，於菩薩無相修，當知獲得。初無相住，於菩薩無相修，當知圓證。第二無相住，於菩薩無相修，當知清淨。無礙解住、最上成滿菩薩住，於菩薩無相修果，當知領受。
items.en:
Furthermore, bodhisattvas at the abode of resolute practice, with respect to a bodhisattva's mark-free cultivation, should be understood as having set forth towards it.
Commentary: Regarding "a bodhisattva's mark-free cultivation" — this refers to the language-transcending nature of all phenomena. The mark of genuine reality is called mark-free, one should understand.
Bodhisattvas at the abodes of utmost joy, excellent moral discipline, excellent mind, and excellent wisdom, with respect to a bodhisattva's mark-free cultivation, should be understood as having attained it.
Bodhisattvas at the first mark-free abode, with respect to a bodhisattva's mark-free cultivation, should be understood as having fully realised it.
Bodhisattvas at the second mark-free abode, with respect to a bodhisattva's mark-free cultivation, should be understood as having purified it.
Bodhisattvas at the abode of unobstructed understanding and the most excellent, fully accomplished bodhisattva abode, with respect to the fruit of a bodhisattva's mark-free cultivation, should be understood as receiving it.

items.title: Section: An Eleven-Part Deep Dive Opens — What Conduct, State, and Mark Characterises a Bodhisattva Turning Within the Abode of Resolute Practice?

items.zh: 問：勝解行住菩薩轉時，應知何行、何狀、何相？
items.en:
Question: When a bodhisattva turns within the abode of resolute practice, what conduct, what state, and what mark should be understood as characterising that bodhisattva?
Commentary: Regarding "what conduct, what state, and what mark should be understood" — conduct refers to setting forth; state refers to attaining; mark refers to the natural outflow. As explained further below: the practices capable of leading into realisation are called conduct; the moment of actually entering it is called attaining; and, once one has entered, the fruit and benefit brought to full, complete realisation is called the natural outflow. This same sequence of correspondence should be understood accordingly; everything that follows should be explained according to this same standard.

items.title: Section: Not Yet Spontaneous, Not Yet Firmly Settled — and Five Fears an Ordinary Bodhisattva Has Not Yet Overcome

items.zh: 答：勝解行住菩薩轉時，思擇力勝；於諸菩薩所作加行，以分別慧數數思擇方能修作，未能任性成辦所作。未得堅固相續無退菩薩勝修。如於勝修，於勝修果種種無礙勝解、神通、解脫、等持、等至，亦未能得。未能超越五種怖畏。謂不活畏、惡名畏、死畏、惡趣畏、處眾怯畏。
items.en:
Answer: When a bodhisattva turns within the abode of resolute practice, the power of discerning reflection predominates; with respect to the applied efforts proper to a bodhisattva, only by means of discriminating wisdom, reflecting again and again, can such efforts actually be carried out — not yet able to accomplish what needs to be done spontaneously, as a matter of course.
Such a bodhisattva has not yet attained the firm, continuous, irreversible superior cultivation of a bodhisattva.
Commentary: Regarding "not yet attained the firm, continuous, irreversible superior cultivation of a bodhisattva" — what is undertaken with settled resolve is called firm. What is undertaken without any gap is called continuous. Whatever is attained, never again regressing, is called irreversible. The abode of utmost joy possesses this pattern of cultivation, which is why it is called superior cultivation. The abode of resolute practice has not yet manifested this, which is why it is said to have not yet attained it.
Just as with superior cultivation itself, such a bodhisattva has likewise not yet attained superior cultivation's own various fruits — unobstructed understanding, resolute understanding, supernormal knowledge, liberation, concentration, and meditative attainment.
Such a bodhisattva has not yet transcended five kinds of fear — namely, fear of not surviving, fear of ill repute, fear of death, fear of falling into an unfortunate rebirth, and fear of timidity before an assembly.

items.title: Section: Compassion That Still Requires Effort, Occasional Lapses Into Wrong Conduct, and Trust in the Three Jewels Not Yet Personally Verified

items.zh: 於所應作利有情事，策勵思惟方能修作，未能任性哀愍愛念。或於一時，於諸有情，由身語意發起邪行；或於一時，於諸境界發起貪著；或於一時，於資生具現有慳悋。信他諸佛菩薩而行，未能自內了知真實。謂於如來、或法、或僧、或真實義、或有情事、或佛菩薩神通威力、或因、或果、或應得義、或得方便、或於所行皆隨他信。成就狹小聞所成智、思所成智，而非無量。
items.en:
With respect to what should be done to benefit sentient beings, such a bodhisattva must consciously exhort and reflect before being able to act, not yet able to give rise spontaneously to compassionate, loving concern. At times, such a bodhisattva may still give rise, through body, speech, or mind, to wrongful conduct towards beings; at times may give rise to attachment towards some object; at times may display genuine stinginess regarding material possessions.
Such a bodhisattva acts on trust in the buddhas and bodhisattvas, not yet having personally, inwardly realised the truth.
This means that, with respect to the tathagata, or the teaching, or the community, or genuine reality, or the maturation of beings, or the buddhas' and bodhisattvas' own supernormal power, or cause, or result, or what is to be attained, or the means of attainment, or with respect to one's own conduct, such a bodhisattva follows entirely on trust in what has been taught by others, thereby accomplishing only a narrow wisdom of hearing and a narrow wisdom of reflection, not yet boundless wisdom.

items.title: Section: Teachings Sometimes Forgotten, and Aspiration Towards Great Awakening Not Yet Vigorous, Firm, or Unshakeable

items.zh: 又即於此或時忘失，有忘失法。成就菩薩苦遲通行，於大菩提無猛利樂欲，無熾然精進，無有甚深牢固淨信。
items.en:
Furthermore, precisely within this same narrow wisdom, there are times when it is simply forgotten — there is a genuine capacity for forgetting.
Such a bodhisattva belongs to the class whose progress towards awakening is painful and slow, holding no vigorous eagerness towards great awakening, no blazing diligence, and no profound, unshakeable, pure faith regarding it.
Commentary: Regarding "no vigorous eagerness towards great awakening" and the like — the Chapter on Maturation explains: when a bodhisattva abides in middling-grade maturity, there is then middling-grade eagerness and middling-grade applied effort. Reaching all the way to the boundary of the second incalculable eon, such a bodhisattva's blazing, unshakeable factors of awakening have already become joined with wholesome qualities. Within this, because the disposition itself has become genuinely deep and sincere, and extremely vigorous, capable of producing a superior, vast result and great benefit, this is called blazing. Because there is no turning back, no falling into regression, and constant, superior advancement, this is called unshakeable. The present bodhisattva at the abode of resolute practice, however, abides in lesser-grade maturity, possessing only lesser-grade eagerness and lesser-grade applied effort — this is why it is said such a bodhisattva has no vigorous eagerness and no blazing diligence. Since there is still the possibility of turning back and falling into regression, such a bodhisattva is not yet unshakeable — this is why it is said such a bodhisattva has no profound, unshakeable, pure faith.

blocks.text: Each abode is named for what defines it. Then the treatise turns, with real candour, to describe the bodhisattva who has not yet reached the first ground: fearful, inconsistent, still needing effort for everything.
"Relying on the concentration underlying worldly pure wisdom, to awaken to the truths." Venerable Miào Jìng: this shows insight is cultivated within concentration.

subs.head: Named by wisdom or by object

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi: the abode of the factors of awakening is named for the observing wisdom; the abode of the truths is named for the object observed.
Venerable Miào Jìng: 加行 really means effort; if afflictions arise while practising calm and insight, that is a gap.
"Discerning the approaches, meaning, explanatory terms, and distinctions of all phenomena": the four unobstructed understandings again.
"Narrow in scope, incomplete, unsettled, and what is gained can regress." Venerable Miào Jìng: today they can do it, tomorrow maybe not.

Master Cháng Bǎi: observing that the verbally-labelled nature of all phenomena is unfindable is mark-free cultivation. "The first mark-free abode fully realises it; the second purifies it." Venerable Miào Jìng: at that point there is no effort, so it is purer still.

Fear of not surviving, of ill repute, of death, of lower rebirth, and of timidity before assemblies. Master Cháng Bǎi: though giving, they hoard for fear of not getting by; in front of crowds they appear timid.
Venerable Miào Jìng: without realising ultimate truth, with a grasping mind, one's scope is narrow. Master Cháng Bǎi: such bodhisattvas rely only on faith in the buddhas' teachings.
"Today they can do it, tomorrow maybe not." This is a portrait of most practitioners, and the treatise draws it without contempt. Inconsistency is a stage, not a verdict.

quiz.q: The abode of wisdom associated with the factors of awakening relies on what, and aims at what?
options: relying on the concentration underlying worldly pure wisdom, to awaken to the truths, discerning the thirty-seven factors
quiz.why: "Relying on the concentration underlying worldly pure wisdom, to awaken to the truths, abiding in discernment of the thirty-seven factors." Venerable Miào Jìng: this shows insight is cultivated within concentration.

quiz.q: How do the lectures distinguish the naming of "factors-associated" and "truths-associated" wisdom abodes?
options: both: the first named for the observing wisdom, the second for the observed object (the truths)
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the factors of awakening are the observing wisdom, and the abode is named for it; the truths abode is named for the observed object. Venerable Miào Jìng agrees.

quiz.q: In "the mark-free abode with effort," how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "effort" and "gaps"?
options: "加" means effort; if afflictions arise during calm and insight, that is a gap
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "加" really means effort; if your afflictions arise while practising calm and insight, that's a gap. Master Cháng Bǎi: effort and application still needed, with frequent intention.

quiz.q: The abode of unobstructed understanding discerns which four aspects of phenomena?
quiz.why: "Discerning the approaches, meaning, explanatory terms, and distinctions of all phenomena." Venerable Miào Jìng: approaches are unobstructed dharma-eloquence, meaning is meaning-eloquence, explanatory terms language-eloquence.

quiz.q: At the abode of resolute practice, what is a bodhisattva's cultivation of the perfections like?
options: narrow, incomplete, unsettled — what's gained can regress
quiz.why: "Narrow in scope, incomplete, unsettled, and what is gained can regress." Venerable Miào Jìng: today they can do it, tomorrow maybe not.

quiz.q: In the five stages of mark-free cultivation, what are the first and second mark-free abodes?
options: the first fully realises; the second purifies
quiz.why: "The first mark-free abode fully realises mark-free cultivation; the second purifies it." Venerable Miào Jìng: at that point there's no effort, so it's purer still.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "mark-free" in "mark-free cultivation"?
options: observing that the verbally-labelled nature of all phenomena is unfindable
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: observing that the verbally-labelled nature of all phenomena is unfindable is mark-free cultivation. Venerable Miào Jìng: seeing the ultimate truth is called mark-free.

quiz.q: Which five fears has the resolute-practice bodhisattva not yet overcome?
options: fear of not surviving, ill repute, death, lower rebirth, timidity in assemblies
quiz.why: Fear of not surviving, of ill repute, of death, of lower rebirth, and of timidity before assemblies. Master Cháng Bǎi: though giving, they hoard for fear of not getting by; in front of crowds they appear timid.

quiz.q: "…or the matters of beings — all trusted on others' word." How do the lectures read "matters of beings"?
options: Miào Jìng: beings' affairs are delusion, karma, suffering — without realising ultimate truth one's view is narrow; Cháng Bǎi: outer-ordinary bodhisattvas are still "outside the principle," relying on faith in the teachings
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: beings' affairs are delusion, karma, and suffering; without realising ultimate truth, with a grasping mind, one's scope is narrow. Master Cháng Bǎi: outer-ordinary bodhisattvas' minds are still outside the principle, relying only on faith in the buddhas' teachings.
